scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw DFT outputs requires re-running DFT calculations, which is infeasible in the verifier sandbox. Therefore we compare the agent's reported scalar values against the paper's published reference values with asymmetric tolerances (lower is better) and verify structural ordering.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden gold values for the seven DFT-derived quantities used in scoring
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper reported values in Figure 3 and main text: ΔE(C1) vacuum 0.73 eV, ΔE(C2) vacuum 0.87 eV, ΔE(C1) with cations averaged 0.54 eV, ΔE(C2) with cations averaged 0.18 eV, OCCO adsorption shift -1.2 eV, 2CO adsorption shift -0.4 eV, OCCOH adsorption shift -1.16 eV.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Direct transcription from the published manuscript (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2017, DOI:10.1021/jacs.7b10142) without modification.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact reported numbers from the original paper, confirmed against the manuscript text and Supporting Information; unused for any other purpose.

outputs.description: Headline DFT reaction energies and cation-induced adsorption energy shifts on Cu(100) for CO reduction intermediates.

output_contract.notes: Scoring compares each value to a hidden gold threshold (meeting or beating the reference) and verifies the relative energetic ordering: C2_with_cations < C1_with_cations < C1_vacuum ≈ C2_vacuum, and |OCCO_shift| > |OCCOH_shift| > |2CO_shift|.

steps.description: Verify all seven DFT-derived energies against paper gold with directional tolerances and check structural ordering of the energies.
